messages.content: Draft an HHVC Transaction page for bed bug complaints. Use this exact heading format: PAGE NAME:, PAGE TYPE:, PRIMARY USER:. Include clear next steps and mention 311.

judgeSamples.output:
# Bed Bug Complaint Draft — Karl CMS Transaction Page

---

**PAGE NAME:** Report a Bed Bug Problem
**PAGE TYPE:** Transaction
**PRIMARY USER:** A renter, tenant, or building resident who has discovered bed bugs in their home and needs to file a complaint with the City.

---

## Why This Is a Transaction Page

This page drives the user to **do something with the City** — file a complaint. Per the Karl editor guidance on choosing content types, a Transaction page is the correct choice here because it is the entry point into a City service and must be actionable.
📎 https://sfdigitalservices.gitbook.io/karl-sf.gov-editor-help-center/using-karl-the-cms/content-types/choosing-a-content-type

---

## PAGE DRAFT

---

### Report a Bed Bug Problem

Bed bugs are a health and housing issue. If you have bed bugs in your rental unit and your landlord has not addressed the problem, you can file a complaint with the City.

---

### What You Can Do

**Call or go online to file a complaint with 311.**

San Francisco 311 connects you to City services. When you report a bed bug problem, your complaint is routed to the **Department of Building Inspection (DBI)** or the **San Francisco Department of Public Health (SFDPH)**, depending on the nature of the issue.

---

### Before You Start

Have this information ready when you contact 311:

- Your full address, including unit number
- The date you first noticed the bed bugs
- Whether you have already notified your landlord in writing
- Any photos or documentation you have (useful but not required)

---

### How to File a Complaint

**Step 1 — Contact 311**
Call **3-1-1** (or 415-701-2311 from outside San Francisco), go to **sf311.org**, or use the **SF311 mobile app** to submit your complaint online.

**Step 2 — Describe the problem**
Tell 311 that you have a bed bug infestation in your rental unit. Include your address, unit number, and a brief description of the problem.

**Step 3 — Notify your landlord in writing (if you haven't already)**
Your landlord is legally responsible for maintaining a habitable unit. Send a written notice — email or letter — describing the problem and keeping a copy for your records.

**Step 4 — Schedule an inspection**
After your complaint is filed, a City inspector may contact you to schedule an inspection of your unit. You will typically receive a case or complaint number — keep this for your records.

**Step 5 — Follow up**
If you do not hear back within 5–7 business days, follow up with 311 using your complaint number.

---

### After You File

- A **DBI or SFDPH inspector** may visit your building to assess the infestation
- Your landlord may be required to hire a **licensed pest control professional**
- If violations are found, the City can issue a **Notice of Violation** to the property owner

---

## SUPPORTING INFORMATION SECTIONS

*(These appear in expandable or static sections near the bottom of the page. The "Supporting information" label does not display publicly.)*
📎 https://sfdigitalservices.gitbook.io/karl-sf.gov-editor-help-center/using-karl-the-cms/content-types/building-a-page-by-content-type/transaction/supporting-information-on-a-transaction-page

---

**Your rights as a tenant**
San Francisco law requires landlords to provide and maintain habitable housing. This includes addressing pest infestations. If your landlord fails to act after written notice, you may have additional legal options. Contact the **Rent Board** or a tenant legal services organization for help.

**About bed bugs**
Bed bugs are small insects that feed on human blood, usually at night. They hide in mattresses, furniture, and walls. An infestation is not a sign of poor cleanliness — they spread through travel, used furniture, and shared walls in multi-unit buildings.

**Protecting yourself during treatment**
Cooperate with your landlord's pest control provider. You may need to prepare your unit before treatment, such as laundering bedding and clearing clutter. Ask the pest control professional for written preparation instructions.

---

## RELATED PAGES (Right Rail)

*(Only Transaction, Information, Campaign, and Topic pages can be tagged as Related. Titles and descriptions sync automatically when linked pages are updated.)*
📎 https://sfdigitalservices.gitbook.io/karl-sf.gov-editor-help-center/using-karl-the-cms/components/related

Suggested Related pages to tag:

| Page Title | Content Type |
|---|---|
| Report a housing code violation | Transaction |
| Tenant rights in San Francisco | Information |
| Contact your landlord about repairs | Information |
| San Francisco Rent Board | Transaction |

---

## EDITOR NOTES

> 📝 **Content type check:** This is correctly filed as a **Transaction** because the primary action is filing a complaint with the City via 311. If you build a deeper explainer about what bed bugs are or tenant legal options, create a separate **Information** page and use the **Part of** component to link it back to this Transaction page.
> 📎 https://sfdigitalservices.gitbook.io/karl-sf.gov-editor-help-center/using-karl-the-cms/content-types/building-a-page-by-content-type/information/part-of-on-an-information-page

> 📝 **311 integration:** Confirm with your 311 team the correct service request category name so the CTA language exactly matches what users will see in the 311 system.

> 📝 **Department ownership:** Confirm whether DBI or SFDPH is the primary owning department for this complaint type before publishing, and update the routing language accordingly.

messages.content: Create an HHVC Information page about mold prevention for tenants. Keep language simple, and preserve headings PAGE NAME:, PAGE TYPE:, PRIMARY USER:.

judgeSamples.output:
# Mold Prevention in Your Rental Home

**PAGE NAME:** Mold Prevention in Your Rental Home
**PAGE TYPE:** Information
**PRIMARY USER:** Renters/Tenants

---

## Page Summary

Learn how to prevent mold in your home and what to do if you find it.

---

## Body Content

### What is mold?

Mold is a fungus that grows in wet or damp places. It can appear as black, green, or white spots. Mold can make you and your family sick.

### Where does mold grow?

Mold likes:

* Bathrooms and kitchens
* Under sinks and around pipes
* Windows and walls where moisture builds up
* Basements and crawl spaces

### How to prevent mold

**Control moisture in your home:**

* Use the bathroom fan when you shower or bathe
* Use the kitchen fan when you cook
* Open windows when the weather allows
* Wipe up spills and leaks right away
* Do not let wet clothes or towels sit in piles

**Watch for leaks:**

* Check under sinks regularly
* Look for water stains on walls and ceilings
* Report leaks to your landlord right away

**Keep air moving:**

* Leave space between furniture and walls
* Do not block vents or heaters

---

### What to do if you find mold

**Small areas of mold (smaller than a dinner plate):**

You may be able to clean it yourself with soap and water. Wear gloves and a mask. Dry the area completely after cleaning.

**Large areas of mold:**

Do not try to clean large amounts of mold yourself. Contact your landlord in writing. Your landlord is responsible for fixing the conditions that caused the mold.

---

### Know your rights

San Francisco tenants have the right to a safe and livable home. If your landlord does not fix a mold problem, you may have options, including:

* Contacting the Department of Building Inspection
* Filing a complaint with the Rent Board

---

## Part of

> This Information page should be linked to the **Report a Housing Code Violation** Transaction page using the *Part of* component.
>
> Per Karl CMS guidance, the **Part of** component lets you choose exactly one SF.gov Transaction page that this Information page supports.
> 📎 [Part of on an Information page](https://sfdigitalservices.gitbook.io/karl-sf.gov-editor-help-center/using-karl-the-cms/content-types/building-a-page-by-content-type/information/part-of-on-an-information-page)

---

## Content Type Note

> This page is built as an **Information** page because it provides reference content — tenants are not completing a transaction directly on this page. If the primary goal were to prompt a user to take action with the City (such as filing a complaint), a **Transaction** page would be more appropriate.
>
> 📎 [Choosing a content type](https://sfdigitalservices.gitbook.io/karl-sf.gov-editor-help-center/using-karl-the-cms/content-types/choosing-a-content-type)

output.summary: Transaction page has correct type and includes required sections, but lacks actionable first-person title, uses passive voice and hidden verbs, omits Related pages, and needs plain-language improvements.
passed: Page type is valid Karl content type: Transaction
What to know and What to do sections present for Transaction page
311 reference included in What to do section
System Relationships correctly lists parent as Topic
All components used are valid Karl components (What to know, What to do, Phone number reference implicit)
warnings: Title is not action-oriented or first-person — change 'Report bed bugs in your apartment' to 'Report bed bugs in my apartment' or 'I want to report bed bugs in my apartment'
Sentence 'We inspect for signs of infestation' contains hidden verb — use 'We look for signs of infestation' instead
First sentence of What to know does not lead with main point for tenant action — consider starting with 'You should report bed bugs quickly because they spread in shared housing'

What to do section does not address reader as 'you' — rewrite 'Call 311 to file a complaint' as 'You can call 311 to file a complaint' and 'Keep records of bites and sightings' as 'You should keep records of your bites and sightings'

Missing Related pages component — per https://sfdigitalservices.gitbook.io/karl-sf.gov-editor-help-center/using-karl-the-cms/components/related, Transaction pages should include Related pages (which may link to Information, Campaign, or Topic pages that support this transaction)
Tenant responsibilities not explicitly addressed — add a section clarifying tenant duties (e.g., providing access for inspection, documenting evidence)
failed: Passive voice used once — 'We inspect for signs of infestation' is passive; rewrite as active voice 'We look for infestation signs'
Description uses institutional voice 'so we can' — rewrite to lead with your benefit: 'Get your home inspected for bed bugs' (18 characters) to be more user-centered
